objections.definitionEvidence: Find at least one instance of the named defect, including unfamiliar wording. Several checks can legitimately label the same passage; another useful detail or defect supplies no automatic exemption.

draftEvidence.true: At least one cue supplies generic emotional atmosphere
draftEvidence.false: The candidate supplies literal sound conditions, purposeful quiet, consequential withholding of speech, an informative figurative relation, specific interpersonal meaning or another identifiable function, or no eligible scene-state cue occurs.

objections.discrepancy: The true criterion quantifies over any defective cue, while the false criterion describes a singular useful candidate. It does not require all eligible candidates to be useful or require zero defined defects.
objections.consequence: For a passage combining purposeful quiet with a separate generic quiet-as-verdict cue, the true criterion fits the defective cue and the false criterion can fit the useful cue. The passage-level choice is ambiguous.
objections.mitigatingText: The body says another useful detail protects only its own contribution. The question and body support the correct any-instance reading, but the false criterion should express that same scope.
objections.proposedChange: Require that no instance meets the definition, or that every eligible candidate has one of the protected functions. Retain the existing no-eligible-cue branch.
